ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.claim: Asad reports that some authorities date the surah to early Mecca, while others consider it more likely to belong to the last group of Meccan revelations.
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.anchor: others regard it as more probable that it belongs to the last group of Meccan revelations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.claim: Al-Infiṭār is the counterpart of al-Takwīr, sharing its intrinsic and extrinsic form, style, meanings, and opening cataclysm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.anchor: great similarity between the intrinsic and extrinsic form, style and meanings of both sūrahs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.claim: Both sūrahs address rich, arrogant Quraysh who ignored the warnings because they trusted their castles and edifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.anchor: The real addressees of both sūrahs are the rich and arrogant among the Quraysh who were turning a deaf ear to the warnings of the Qur’ ān just because they thought that no one would be able to break into their castles and edifices.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.claim: Al-Takwīr reasons from the Qur’an’s authenticity, source, revelation, and bearer; its rejecters cannot distinguish radiant dawn from murky night.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.anchor: the bearer are all pure and upright.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.claim: Al-Infiṭār instead reasons from God’s creativity, power, wisdom, justice, and mercy: signs of power and mercy in humans entail a coming day of reward and punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.claim: Resurrection is no difficulty for God: if first creation was easy, creating again is no harder, and the coming day is certain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.anchor: creating again be difficult for Him?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.claim: God’s present respite for criminals gives them time to reform; those who refuse have no excuse or justification at Judgment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.claim: Divine delay does not mean words and deeds are hidden: angels have been assigned to everyone to record everything.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.anchor: This delay from God should not mislead people to think that their words or deeds are hidden from Him. He has deputed His angels on every person who are noting down each and everything.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.claim: Human formation displays divine power, wisdom, mercy, and justice, showing that Judgment is possible and that human existence has purpose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.anchor: With reference to the grandeur of divine attributes of power, wisdom, mercy and justice found in the formation of a human being a reminder is sounded that no one should think that the Day of Judgement is beyond the power of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r1.claim: God’s power, creativity, care, and wisdom in creating humanity show that He acted purposefully and will hold people accountable, resurrecting and judging them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r1.anchor: power, creativity, thoroughness and wisdom in creating

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r2.claim: The creation vocabulary spans making or sketching and creating, then perfecting; the verses thus allude to humanity’s initial and final stages of formation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r2.anchor: “to make a sketch of something” and “to create something”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r3.claim: Humanity reflects God’s brilliant creativity and must pass through tests to its appointed fate; refusal to face that responsibility merits punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r3.anchor: a reflection of the brilliant creativity of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r4.claim: The human midpoint among creations makes people worthy of vicegerency and the status of the middle community; fulfilling this duty merits the eternal kingdom of Heaven.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r4.anchor: is worthy of being made the vicegerent of God on earth

QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11.claim: God fitted the body's limbs according to wise designs, varying beauty and ugliness, and height and shortness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11.anchor: ركب أعضاءك على الوجوه الحكمية { فى أى صورة ما شآء } ، من الحسن والقبح ، والطول والقصر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r16.claim: God creates the person, gives bodily form, and equips each part with its intended benefit; He proportioned the temperament and balanced the structure.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r16.anchor: { الذي خلقك } أي أوجدك من العدم مهيئا لتقدير الأعضاء { فسواك } عقب تلك الأطوار بتصوير الأعضاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r17.speaker: الكوفيون
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r17.claim: The Kufan lightened reading of ‘fa-ʿadalaka’ means God turned the person away from deformity and made the form upright.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r17.anchor: وكذا العدل في قراءة الكوفيين بالتخفيف أي فأمالك عن تشويه الخلقة وتقبيح الصورة , وجعلك معتدلا في صورتك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r18.claim: Creation and bodily proportion require gratitude and fear, since the one who can proportion a person can also disfigure or punish them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r18.anchor: وكل هذا يقتضي غاية الشكر والخوف منه إن عصى , لأنه كما قدر على التسوية يقدر على التشويه وغيره من العذاب

NAHHAS:v5p169/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p169/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p169/r1.claim: A cited line says the two sides killed equal numbers; another interpretation of عدلك is that God shaped you as He willed, in beauty or ugliness, health or illness.
NAHHAS:v5p169/r1.anchor: ( وعدلنا مثل بدر فاعتدل ) أي قتلنا منهم مثل من قتلوا منا وقد قيل عدلك أمالك إلى ما شاء من حسن وقبيح

TABRISI:82:19/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:19/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:82:19/r1.claim: The Kufan readers and Abu Ja'far use the light reading of fa-ʿadalaka; the other readers double the d, yielding the sense that God shaped the creature's form.
TABRISI:82:19/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر فعدلك خفيفة والباقون بالتشديد

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r14.claim: God created the human from a drop when he was nothing, then formed him into a hearing, seeing person and made him balanced.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r14.anchor: { الذي خلقك } من نطفة ولم تك شيئا { فسواك } إنسانا تسمع وتبصر { فعدلك } أي جعلك معتدلا

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r15.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r15.claim: Muqatil explains that God proportioned the person's two eyes, ears, hands, and feet, with neither of each pair out of balance with its counterpart.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r15.anchor: عدل خلقك في العينين والأذنين واليدين والرجلين عن مقاتل

STUDYQURAN:82:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:7/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:82:7/r1.claim: Fashioning refers to making human parts and faculties sound and functional.
STUDYQURAN:82:7/r1.anchor: Fashioned you refers to the manner in which God has made all human parts and faculties sound and functional

STUDYQURAN:82:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:7/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:82:7/r2.claim: The text's ʿaddalaka can also be read ʿadalaka, turned, meaning God can turn people in any direction; both readings work, but ʿaddalaka is grammatically better if verse 8 continues verse 7.
STUDYQURAN:82:7/r2.anchor: meaning “turned you,” implying that God turns people in any direction

STUDYQURAN:82:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r3.speaker: Qu and R
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r3.claim: Verses 7–8 can refer to inner qualities, such as states of faith or disobedience, rather than outer form.
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r3.anchor: Vv. 7–8 can also be taken to imply the inner qualities rather than the outer form, thus referring to states of faith or disobedience

STUDYQURAN:82:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r4.claim: The verses can also refer to states of felicity or wretchedness, commonly understood as salvation and damnation.
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r4.anchor: which are commonly understood as referring to states of damnation and salvation

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r1.claim: The phrase says God created and fashioned the human; the Medinan, Meccan, Syrian, and Basran readers recite fa-ʿaddalaka with a doubled dal, while most Kufans recite fa-ʿadalaka with a light dal.

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r2.speaker: من قرأ بالتشديد
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r2.claim: The doubled form means making the human balanced, upright, and proportionate in creation.

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r3.speaker: من قرأ بالتخفيف
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r3.claim: The light form means turning or directing the human to whichever image God wills, beautiful, ugly, or resembling a relative.
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r3.anchor: وكأن الذين قرءوه بالتخفيف، وجهوا معنى الكلام إلى صرفك، وأمالك إلى أي صورة شاء

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r4.claim: He accepts both established readings as sound and correct, but prefers the doubled form because Arabic more naturally uses في with adjustment than with turning or directing.
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r4.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك عندي بالصواب أن يقال: إنهما قراءتان معروفتان في قراءة الأمصار، صحيحتا المعنى

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r1.claim: In a sound hadith, God draws the believer near, covers him, asks him to acknowledge his sins until he fears ruin, then says He concealed them in this life and forgives him today.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r1.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح) : إن الله يدني المؤمن فيضع عليه كنفه

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r2.claim: The description of God as creator further establishes His lordship and explains His generosity: giving existence is better than nonexistence, and the ability to originate implies the ability to recreate.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r2.anchor: {الذى خلقك} صفة ثانية مقررة للربوبية مبينة للكرم لأن الخلق إعطاء لوجود

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r3.claim: God made the limbs sound and balanced so each performs its intended benefit, such as grasping by the hand, walking by the foot, and seeing by the eye.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r3.anchor: أي جعل أعضاءك سوية سليمة معدة لمنفعها أي بحيث يترتب على كل عضو

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r4.claim: God balanced corresponding limbs and features, such as the two hands, legs, ears, eyes, and sides of the body, without disproportion.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r4.anchor: عدل بعض تلك الأعضاء ببعض بحيث أعتدلت ولم تتفاوت مثل أن تكون إحدى اليدين

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r5.claim: Anatomists say the two sides of the body match in bones, shape, veins, arteries, and nerves.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r5.anchor: قال علماء التشريح إنه تعالى ركب جانبي هذه الجنة على التساوي

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, ʿadalaka means He turned you away from an ugly animal form and gave you a beautiful form distinct from other creatures, as in 95:4.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r6.anchor: ويقال عدله عن الطرق أي صرفه فيكون المعنى فصرفك عن الخلقة المكروهة

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r7.claim: A variant with doubled dāl, faʿaddalaka, means that God made the human being proportionate and harmonious without disparity, close in sense to the lighter form.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r7.anchor: وقرىء فعدلك بالتشديد أي صيرك معتدلا متناسب الخلق من غير تفاوت

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r8.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r8.claim: Al-Junayd says God perfected the human form through knowledge and adjusted it through faith.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r8.anchor: وقال الجنيد قدس سره تسوية الخلقة بلمعرفة وتعديلها بالإيمان

BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r9.speaker: ذو النون
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r9.claim: Dhū al-Nūn says God brought the human being into existence and subjected all created things to him, without subjecting him to any of them.
BURSEVI:v10p277#2/r9.anchor: وقال ذو النون قدس سره أوجدك فسخر لك المكونات أجمع ولم يسخرك لشيء

THALABI:v10p147/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p147/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة
THALABI:v10p147/r1.claim: The Kufans lighten the dāl in “ʿadalaka,” meaning God turned and inclined a person toward whatever form He willed, beautiful or ugly, short or tall.
THALABI:v10p147/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة بتخفيف الدال أي صرفك وأمالك إلى أي صورة شاء قبيحا أو جميلا وقصيرا أو طويلا

THALABI:v10p147/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p147/r2.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيد
THALABI:v10p147/r2.claim: The other readers double the dāl: God made the person’s creation upright and balanced; al-Farra and Abu Ubayd prefer this reading, citing 95:4.
THALABI:v10p147/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتشديد أي قومك وجعلك معتدل الخلق، وهو اختيار الفراء وأبي عبيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r1.claim: God created the human from a drop after he was nothing, then formed him as a man with hearing and sight.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains fa-ʿadalaka as making the human proportionate in form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: جعلك معتدلا، معدل (¬6) الخلق (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī says God fashioned the human in the fairest form and finely proportioned him, enabling capacities unavailable to others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r3.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: عدل خلقك فأخرجك في أحسن تقويم، وهيأ فيك بلطف الخلقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, says God made the human upright, proportionate, and beautiful in appearance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r4.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: جعلك قائما معتدلا حسن الصورة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r5.claim: Muqātil says God proportioned the paired eyes, ears, hands, and feet, without making all of the human one undifferentiated form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يريد (عدل) (¬2) خلقك في العينين، والأذنين، واليدين، والرجلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r6.claim: On this explanation, God balanced the paired human limbs among the several organs He created.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا المعنى عدل بين ما خلق لك من الأعضاء التي في الإنسان منها اثنان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r7.claim: The Kufans read fa-ʿadalaka with a light dāl rather than the doubled form.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the light reading as turning the person toward any image God wills, but prefers the doubled reading: Arabic permits عدلك إلى كذا, not عدلتك فيه; the light reading also makes في أي صورة attach weakly to fa-ʿadalaka.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r8.anchor: قال الفراء: ووجهه فصرفك (¬5) إلى أي صورة شاء، قال: والتشديد أحسن الوجهين؛ لأنك تقول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbayd likewise gives an argument for preferring the doubled reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r9.anchor: ونحو هذا ذكر أبو عبيد حجة لاختيار التشديد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r10.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r10.claim: Abū ʿAlī answers that the light reading means proportioning the parts to one another, leaving a balanced, harmonious form without disparity; it avoids al-Farrāʾ's objection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p294/r10.anchor: وقال أبو علي (¬1): على معنى التخفيف عدل بعضه ببعض فكنت معتدل الخلقة متناسبها، فلا تفاوت فيها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r7.claim: God made the human’s creation proportionate and upright in form and stature.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r7.anchor: { الذي خلقك فسواك } جعلك مستوي الخلق { فعدلك } قومك وجعلك معتدل الخلق والقامة.

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r26.claim: Here “created” means bringing into existence initially, as it precedes shaping, balancing, forming, and composing the human being.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r26.anchor: O Rabbin ki seni halketti burada “halk”

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r27.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r27.claim: Existence, the foundation of every blessing, is the first instance of the Lord’s generosity.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r27.anchor: Ve mâlum ki her nimetin esası olan vücud

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r28.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r28.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r28.claim: God develops the human through stages to human maturity, fit to receive the spirit, and orders and perfects the body, limbs, and faculties.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r28.anchor: bünyeni, a‘zâlarını, kuvvelerini düzenine koydu, düzgünleştirdi

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r29.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r29.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r29.claim: The phrase means that God gave the human proportion, balance, and moderation.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r29.anchor: İkisi de bir mânaya olarak denkleştirmek ve mutedil kılmak

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r30.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r30.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r30.claim: Two readings use a light or doubled dāl, from ʿadl or taʿdīl; both mean balancing and making moderate, completing the account of human formation.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r30.anchor: Burada biri “adl”den dâl’ın feth u tahfîfiyle

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r31.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r31.speaker: Mukātil
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r31.claim: Muqatil explains the phrase as symmetry of paired organs and proportion throughout the body, like the balancing of fingertips in Qiyama 75:4; the author says this does not distinctly express human uniqueness.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r31.anchor: Mukātil’den rivayet edildiğine göre göz, kulak, el, ayak gibi çift a‘zâların denkliği

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r32.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r32.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r32.claim: Atā transmits Ibn Abbas’s view that God straightened the human back and made him upright, unlike crooked-backed beasts; the author finds its human specificity and place after shaping clearer.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r32.anchor: Atâ’nın İbn Abbas’tan rivayet ettiği vecihte ise “belini doğrulttu, kāim mutedil kıldı, eğri belli behâim gibi yapmadı”

ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r1.speaker: Ebû Ali Fârisî
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r1.claim: Al-Farisi explains “made you balanced” as encompassing the best form, human capacity for reason, thought, and power, and the resulting superiority over other creatures and bodies.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r1.anchor: Üçüncüsü, Ebû Ali Fârisî’nin beyânına göre

ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r2.claim: The human capacities and excellence described in the preceding interpretation are all forms of divine generosity, in keeping with Hijr 15:29 and Isra 17:70.

ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r3.claim: With light dāl, the phrase is also interpreted as turning, bending, or changing direction.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r3.anchor: Bundan başka tahfif ile فَعَدَلَكَ udûl ettirmek, imâle edip çevirmek mânasına dahi tefsir edilmiştir

ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r4.claim: One possible sense is that God repeatedly turned the human from deficiency and an unsuitable form toward perfection and the best form, expressing successive stages of divine selection.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r4.anchor: Birincisi “noksandan kemâle, mülâyim olmayan suretten mülâyim olan surete çevire çevire en güzel surete getirdi” demek olarak yine ıstıfâ merâtibini ifade etmiş olur

ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, after bringing the human to the best form, God may turn him from perfection to a lower state; this warns those deluded by generosity and supports inference to the Hereafter.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#3/r5.anchor: tesviye ile ahsen-i takvîme getirildikten sonra ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَٰهُ أَسْفَلَ سَٰفِلِينَ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r3.claim: The creation and formation described in verses 7–8 expose the ingratitude of people who owe their bodily and mental faculties, and all other blessings, to their Lord yet are misled into denial and rebellion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r3.anchor: insanın insan olarak varlık alanına çıkışındaki yaratıcı rolü dile getirilmekte; böylece insanın, hayatı boyunca her an yararlanmakta olduğu diğer bütün nimetlerden de önce bedensel ve zihnî melekelerle donatılıp düzgün bir insan olarak dünyaya gelişini kendisine borçlu bulunduğu rabbi hakkında

AKHFASH:v2p570/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p570/r1.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p570/r1.claim: Some read ʿadalaka with a lighter form; he glosses the phrase as God having formed the person in this way.
AKHFASH:v2p570/r1.anchor: قال {فعدلك} أي: كذا خلقك، وبعضهم يخففها

AKHFASH:v2p570/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p570/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p570/r2.claim: On the doubled form, God balanced the person's parts against one another, making him proportionate; this has the same sense as ʿadalaka.
AKHFASH:v2p570/r2.anchor: فمن ثقل {عدلك} فانما يقول "عدل خلقك" و"عدلك" أي: عدل بعضك ببعضك

AKHFASH:v2p570/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p570/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p570/r3.claim: The adjacent identical kāf consonants may assimilate; he also describes when to leave them unassimilated according to whether the first or second letter is vowelled.
AKHFASH:v2p570/r3.anchor: فادغمت لأنهما حرفان مثلان. والمثلان يدغم احدهما في صاحبه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p518#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p518#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p518#5/r1.claim: On the reading fa-ʿadalaka, God fashioned and proportioned your creation.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p518#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p518#5/r2.speaker: من قرأ
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p518#5/r2.claim: A reader who lightens the form fa-ʿadalaka means that God turned the person into whichever form He wished, beautiful or ugly.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p518#5/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ: {فعدلك} بالتخفيف (3) ؛ أراد: صرفك إلى ما شاء من الصور في الحسن والقبح.

NAHHAS:v5p167/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p167/r13.speaker: أهل الحرمين وأهل البصرة وأهل الشام والكوفيون
NAHHAS:v5p167/r13.claim: The Meccan, Medinan, Basran, and Syrian readers use the doubled form; Kufans read the form without doubling.
NAHHAS:v5p167/r13.anchor: قراءة أهل الحرمين وأهل البصرة وأهل الشام وقرأ الكوفيون ( فعدلك ) مخففا

NAHHAS:v5p167/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p167/r14.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p167/r14.claim: Al-Farra objects to the light reading because Arabic normally says عدلته إلى كذا or صرفته إليه, not عدلته في كذا.
NAHHAS:v5p167/r14.anchor: واستبعدها الفراء وإن كانت قراءة أصحابه لأنه إنما يقال عدلته إلى كذا وصرفته إليه ولا يكاد يقال عدلته في كذا

NAHHAS:v5p167/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p167/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p167/r15.claim: Al-Nahhas says al-Farra’s objection is mistaken: the clause ends at فعدلك and في belongs with ركبك, not عدلك.
NAHHAS:v5p167/r15.anchor: قال أبو جعفر فيه وهذا غلط لأن الكلام تام عند فعدلك و في متعلقة بركبك لا بعدلك

NAHHAS:v5p167/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p167/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p167/r16.claim: عدلك means God created the person proportionately, with no person exceeding another in the balance of their form.
NAHHAS:v5p167/r16.anchor: ومعنى عدلك في اللغة خلقاك معتدلا لا يزيد رجل على رجل وكذا سائر خلقك

NAHHAS:v5p167/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p167/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p167/r17.claim: The doubled form may intensify عدل, with the light and doubled forms thus carrying the same sense.
NAHHAS:v5p167/r17.anchor: وقد يكون عدلك تكثير عدلك فيكونان بمعنى واحد

SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r1.claim: الذي خلقك may follow the prior expression as apposition, explanatory apposition, or adjective, or may be detached and read nominative or accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r1.anchor: يحتمل الإتباع على البدل والبيان والنعت، والقطع إلى الرفع أو النصب

SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r2.claim: The Kufans read عدلك with a light د; the other readers double it.
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r2.anchor: قرأ الكوفيون " عدلك، مخففا. والباقون/ مثقلا

SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r3.claim: With doubled د, the verb means making the limbs proportionate, so neither hand nor foot is longer and neither eye wider; it derives from التعديل.
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r3.anchor: فالتثقيل بمعنى: جعلك متناسب الأطراف، فلم يجعل إحدى يديك أو رجليك أطول، ولا إحدى عينيك أوسع، فهو من التعديل

SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r4.claim: The light reading can also mean balancing some limbs against others, or derive from العدول, turning a person into whatever forms and shapes God wills.
SAMIN-DURR:82:7/r4.anchor: وقراءة التخفيف تحتمل هذا، أي: عدل بعض أعضائك ببعض. وتحتمل أن تكون من العدول، أي: صرفك إلى ما شاء من الهيئات والأشكال والأشباه

ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r8.claim: Faʿadalaka means God formed you in the best proportion.

ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r9.claim: Both the light and doubled pronunciations of faʿadalaka are read.

ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n4/r1.claim: Asad says God endowed each person with qualities and abilities suited to that individual's life and environment.
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n4/r1.anchor: endowed thee with all the qualities and abilities relevant to the exigencies of thy individual life and thy environment

ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r1.claim: Asad explains human proportion as including bodily needs and emotional urges alongside intellectual and spiritual perceptions.
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r1.anchor: a being subject to physical needs and emotional urges, and at the same time endowed with intellectual and spiritual perceptions

ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r2.claim: Because both sides of human nature are willed by God, Asad says there is no inherent moral conflict between flesh and spirit.
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r2.anchor: both these aspects of the human condition are - as stressed in the next verse - God-willed and, therefore, morally justified.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p364#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p364#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p364#2/r1.claim: With shadda, God proportioned the person and balanced paired limbs; without shadda, He turned the person into whatever form He willed, tall or short, beautiful or ugly.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p364#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بالتشديد والتخفيف فوجه التشديد فيه قومك وساوى بين ما ازدوج من اعضائك

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p364#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p364#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p364#2/r2.claim: Connecting this to God shaping people in the womb, the author describes three forty-day stages, then an angel mixing the person's soil with the embryo; the excerpt breaks off mid-account.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p364#2/r2.anchor: فمعناه ان النطفة اذا قامت اربعين يوما صارت علقة اربعين يوما ومضغة اربعين يوما

NASHR:v2p398/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p398/r6.speaker: الكوفيون
NASHR:v2p398/r6.claim: The Kufans read fa-ʿadalaka with a light dāl; the remaining readers double it.
NASHR:v2p398/r6.anchor: فعدلك فقرأ الكوفيون بتخفيف الدال، وقرأ الباقون بتشديدها

QIRAAT-ER:82:7:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:82:7:6#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:82:7:6#1/r1.claim: The variant doubles dāl, making the final action Form II: thorough adjustment, rectification, or proportional calibration.
QIRAAT-ER:82:7:6#1/r1.anchor: Vr, mutawatir: Canonical variant doubles the dāl, shifting the final action toward Form II intensification

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر، والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r1.claim: Kufans and Abu Jaʿfar read عدلك lightly, meaning God turned or inclined the person into any desired form, handsome or ugly, tall or short; others double it, meaning He proportioned the creation and limbs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر "فعدلك" بالتخفيف أي صرفك وأمالك إلى أي صورة شاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r2.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r2.claim: The doubled reading means God fashioned the person's creation and limbs in balanced proportion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالتشديد أي قومك وجعلك معتدل الخلق والأعضاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r1.claim: This second description of the Lord confirms His lordship, manifests His generosity, and shows that the One able to create first can create again.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r1.anchor: صفة ثانية مقررة للربوبية مبينة للكرم منبهة على أن من قدر على ذلك أولا قدر عليه ثانيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r2.claim: To form soundly is to make the organs healthy, proportioned, and ready for their uses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r2.anchor: جعل الأعضاء سليمة مسواة معدة لمنافعها

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r3.claim: Adjustment may mean making the bodily structure and organs proportionate, or balancing it with faculties that bring felicity.

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r4.claim: The Kufans read the verb lightly, meaning either that the limbs balance one another or that God distinguished the person from other creatures by his form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r4.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون «فعدلك» بالتخفيف أي عدل بعض أعضائك ببعض حتى اعتدلت

DURR-FULL:v8p438/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet recited the words with the medial consonant doubled; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر والحاكم وصححه من طريق سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ {فسواك فعدلك} مثقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r3.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r3.claim: The majority read فعدّلك with doubled dāl.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r4.claim: The Prophet said the phrase when looking at the crescent; narrators agree he doubled the dāl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r4.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم: إذا نظر إلى الهلال، قال: «آمنت بالذي خلقك فسواك فعدلك» لم يختلف الرواة في شد الدال،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r5.speaker: الكوفيون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r5.claim: The Kufans and other readers read without doubled dāl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r5.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون والحسن وأبو جعفر وطلحة والأعمش وأبو رجاء وعيسى بن عبيد: «فعدلك» بتخفيف الدال،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r6.claim: With the lighter reading, God balanced the human’s limbs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r6.anchor: والمعنى عدل أعضاءك بعضها ببعض أي وازن بينها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r2.claim: God made the human upright and proportionate in stature, with the finest bodily form and appearance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r2.anchor: أي: جعلك سويا معتدل القامة منتصبها، في أحسن الهيئات والأشكال.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r3.speaker: بسر بن جحاش القرشي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r3.claim: Busr ibn Jahhash reports the Prophet's narration of God's rebuke: Adam's child was created, shaped, and made upright, yet lived arrogantly, hoarded and withheld wealth, and only promised charity when death reached the collarbones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r3.anchor: عن بسر بن جحاش القرشي: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بصق يوما في كفه، فوضع عليها أصبعه، ثم قال: "قال الله عز وجل:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r4.speaker: يحيى بن حمزة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r4.claim: Al-Mizzi notes that Yahya ibn Hamza also transmits this report from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysara, corroborating the cited route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r4.anchor: قال شيخنا الحافظ أبو الحجاج المزي: وتابعه يحيى بن حمزة، عن ثور بن يزيد، عن عبد الرحمن بن ميسرة (2) .

JISHUMI:v10p7309/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, ʿAsim, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read fa-ʿadalaka with a light dāl, meaning God turned and inclined the person toward whatever form He willed.
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: فعدلك خفيفة الدال، أي: صرفك وأمالك إلى أي صورة شاء،

JISHUMI:v10p7309/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r5.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and Yaʿqub double the dāl, meaning proportionate stature; al-Farraʾ prefers this because adjustment better fits the form, while ‘to’ fits the light reading.
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ويعقوب، بتشديد الدال، أي: جعلك معتدل القامة، واختاره الفراء؛

JISHUMI:v10p7309/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r13.claim: Taswiya is making something match another’s measure; it may concern outward form or inward character.
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r13.anchor: والتسوية: بجعل الشيء على مقدار غيره، ثم قد يكون في الصورة، ويكون في المعنى، سواه تسوية.

MUQATIL:82:6-13/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r3.claim: God created, proportioned, and set the human upright.

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r20.claim: God formed the human from a drop in the womb, giving him two hands, two feet, two eyes, and the rest of his limbs.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r20.anchor: { الذي خلقك } أي قدر خلقك من نطفة { فسواك } في بطن أمك، وجعل لك يدين ورجلين وعينين وسائر أعضائك

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r21.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r21.claim: The common reading with a doubled dāl means God made the human balanced and well-proportioned; Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim choose it.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r21.anchor: { فعدلك } أي جعلك معتدلا سوي الخلق كما يقال: هذا شيء معدل. وهذه قراءة العامة، وهي اختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم

QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r1.speaker: الكوفيون: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r1.claim: The Kufans Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read the verb lightly: God inclined and directed the human into whatever form He wished, beautiful or ugly, tall or short.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r1.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: «فعدلك» مخففا أي: أمالك وصرفك إلى أي صورة شاء
